title: An Audience with The Scholar
body:
Wenna Aldric receives you standing, at a folding desk set in the road a careful hundred paces from the edge, which is the closest the founder of the Academy has to a door home. Your greeting comes out in the right tense. She notices, and says nothing, which from her is a mark.

On the desk lies her list, seventeen lines in her careful script, fourteen of them struck through.

'You never technically graduated,' she says. 'And yet the only working school in the world answers to you. I have opinions about that. Before you say anything, show me that you know the proper name of what you are about to do.'

choices.label: Unite: ask for her mark
choices.resultText: 'Ask properly.' You do. She takes your student record from the desk, kept current to the day, and writes one word at its foot, where a mark would go: "Promising." She does not say whether you passed. Then she pledges the Aldric Academy to the guild's cause, and asks, precisely and only once, to be walked through the edge to stand in her school for one hour.

choices.label: Coerce: show her the accession list from the Uncatalogued Wing
choices.resultText: She reads the pulled titles until she reaches the one annotated in a small, upright, patient hand. The title is hers. She goes very still. 'So he was in my library.' The Academy complies. Fear has done what standards would not, and she will not thank you for teaching her that.

choices.label: Overthrow: take the Academy by force
choices.resultText: She sets down the pen and dusts the chalk from her sleeves. 'Very well. The examination will be practical.' She fights like a syllabus, escalating by unit. And she grades.

choices.label: Withdraw: this is not the day
choices.resultText: She notes your withdrawal on the list. Everything is on the list. The list will outlast her, which she considers appropriate.

title: An Audience with The Reviser
body:
Master Aurel Pendry receives you at his bench, among the disassembled spells of every school, with his pen set down. You will learn later how rare that is.

'They say your campus holds a sentence that does not end,' he says. 'A working stopped mid-word, that nobody can get at but you. I have revised every text in this world worth the ink.' (And several that were not.) 'I cannot get at that one.'

He waits. There are no miracles, he has written, only observers who lacked the patience to understand what they were watching. He has been patient a very long time.

choices.label: Unite: offer him one hour inside the Second
choices.resultText: 'One hour,' he says. 'I will need all of it.' (He will need more. He will not ask.) The Annotated Circle pledges to the guild's cause, and he asks to be walked through the edge and into the ceremony hall, to stand in front of the one working he cannot revise.

choices.label: Coerce: refuse him entry until he pledges
choices.resultText: His need does the rest. He signs, then revises the agreement's phrasing twice before returning it. Every correction is in your favor. You will spend a long time working out why that frightens you.

choices.label: Overthrow: take his seat by force
choices.resultText: 'A rushed draft,' he says of you, not unkindly, and opens the tome. Mid-fight, your own spells will start coming back annotated in his hand.

choices.label: Withdraw: this is not the day
choices.resultText: He returns to his argument with the page. You were, his posture says, a digression, though he files digressions, and revisits them.

title: An Audience with The Witness
body:
You do not find Hess. You arrive where she is, which is different, and she was there first. A crow shifts its weight on her shoulder. She does not ask why you have come.

She has watched eight endings happen and intervened in none of them. The ninth she walked out of, before the wards broke.

She has already decided whether to trust you. She decided before you entered the region. You are not negotiating. You are confirming her suspicions.

choices.label: Unite: stand and be seen
choices.resultText: A long silence, the kind rivers make. Then she nods, once, the way she nodded to no one on the dais. The Living Compact does not sign, does not seal, does not swear. It simply, from this day, is with you. She asks for one thing, and she asks it of the ground rather than of you: to be walked back into the hall she left.

choices.label: Bargain: ask her price
choices.resultText: The land does not bargain. The crow does not even look at you.

choices.label: Overthrow: take this ground by force
choices.resultText: She does not move. The place you are standing in does. You will fight the valley before you ever reach the woman. And she will not strike first.

choices.label: Withdraw: this is not the day
choices.resultText: She watches you go. Being watched by Hess is not a punishment. It is worse: it is patience.

title: An Audience with The Vessel
body:
Joren Kall hosts the argument the elements have been having since before language, and it is loud today. When he greets you, a second voice finishes the sentence. It is not his. And lately, he will tell you, it has been quoting someone else's lines.

He is not unkind. He is very tired. These things look similar from a distance; up close, the difference is terrible.

'The storm keeps saying things it heard somewhere,' he manages, in one language at a time. 'I know borrowed words when I translate them. Settle this, with me or over me, but settle it soon.'

choices.label: Unite: help him steady the argument
choices.resultText: The table quiets, one voice at a time, until the argument is merely ancient again instead of poisoned. The Elemental Covenant stands with the guild. Joren asks one thing in return, in his own voice only: to stand for one hour somewhere the weather does not move. For that hour he promises you one question of the storm.

choices.label: Coerce: back one element against the rest
choices.resultText: The argument does not resolve; it adjourns. Joren complies hollow-eyed, one voice now louder than all the others together. You did not win the debate. Remember that, later, when you count on his strength.

choices.label: Overthrow: silence the host
choices.resultText: The host falls. The argument does not. What rises when he drops has no chair to sit in, and every voice at once.

choices.label: Withdraw: this is not the day
choices.resultText: The argument resumes before you reach the door. One of its voices says goodbye in a diction you recognize, and wish you did not.

title: An Audience with The Namer
body:
You are shown to a chair that was placed for you before you decided to come. The Namer does not look up from the working on their desk. 'I'm not finished. Sit.'

You count the layers you can see in the working and reach four before the count stops behaving. They have been watching you since before you entered the region. They know what layer you are on. You do not.

At last they set the working aside and fold their hands. 'You are here to resolve me,' they say. 'You think that is layer one. Shall we discuss what the others were?'

choices.label: Unite: accept the interview, all layers
choices.resultText: 'You're not finished either,' they say at the end, which you take as approval. The Seventh Layer pledges to the guild. Cael asks one thing in return, in a single layer: to be walked through your edge, and left alone with your gate for an hour.

choices.label: Coerce: produce the withdrawn conference paper
choices.resultText: They read the proof that four layers once failed them without any expression at all. 'Provenance,' they say. 'Good.' They comply. From this day forward, everything they make for you carries an eighth layer.

choices.label: Overthrow: strip the layers by force
choices.resultText: Each phase of the fight peels one visible layer. It will end at six. You will never see seven. This, too, is architectural.

choices.label: Withdraw: this is not the day
choices.resultText: 'Layer one concludes,' they say, resuming the working. You are not entirely certain the interview stopped when you left.

title: An Audience with The Conductor
body:
The bar is also a funeral home, depending on what you need tonight. The regulars do not breathe, which keeps the room restful. The Conductor pours without being asked and slides the glass across. Accept it. This matters more than it should.

She sets the Long Table's ledger on the bar, beside the shape of yours. Hers is longer. She keeps a good list too.

'Go on, then,' she says. 'Tell me what you came for.'

choices.label: Unite: open your ledger of the honored dead
choices.resultText: She reads every name (all of it, every timeline) and pours one measure for each. It takes all night. At dawn she says only: 'You keep a good list.' The Long Table stands with the guild. On your way out she asks one thing: to be walked through your edge, into the hall where the class she pours for is still standing.

choices.label: Coerce: threaten the bar's quiet
choices.resultText: It is the one lever she has, and you pulled it. She agrees to everything. She will never forgive it, and her regulars have long memories: memory being, in fact, all they have.

choices.label: Overthrow: clear the Long Table
choices.resultText: The Long Table stands up. Every one of them is someone's regular. She will make certain you learn their names.

choices.label: Withdraw: this is not the day
choices.resultText: She takes the untouched glass back without comment and marks something small in the ledger. The tab, apparently, stays open.

title: An Audience with The Engineer
body:
Bram Korro's cart is parked at your threshold with three current projects aboard, one of which is on fire in what appears to be a controlled way. 'That wasn't supposed to do that,' he says, pleased. 'Write it down.'

He has concluded from field reports that the Anchorhold is a device: the most interesting device in the world, running unattended, with no documentation. Half his machines work. The other half are research. He knows the difference matters less than everyone thinks.

He has one question, and it is not about power, territory, or the war. 'Can I take notes?'

choices.label: Unite: let him take notes
choices.resultText: 'Notes,' he says. 'Just notes. I won't touch anything.' He will want to. The Korro Workshop pledges to the guild, and so, for better or worse, does the cart. Then he asks when he can come in. He asks three times, in three different ways, in case one of them works.

choices.label: Coerce: confiscate the cart
choices.resultText: He hands it over without a word and begins rebuilding all three projects from memory that same night. You have his compliance and none of his attention. The data he keeps on you goes in a different notebook now.

choices.label: Overthrow: dismantle the Workshop
choices.resultText: The fight is the research half of the notebook. Half his devices misfire on purpose, in ways that hurt you both. The randomness is authored, and it is taking measurements. He writes between phases.

choices.label: Withdraw: this is not the day
choices.resultText: 'Provisional result,' he says, chalking something on the cart. 'Come back when you have more data. I will also have more data.' It is not a threat. It is worse: it is a hypothesis.
